content:
Alongside the new Mac mini, Apple today officially launched the next-generation Mac Studio. The all-new Mac Studio lineup features M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, with unified memory supporting up to 512GB.

The new Mac Studio models are available for pre-order starting today.

M5 Max Mac Studio

First, Apple released the new Mac Studio powered by the M5 Max, an upgrade from the previous-generation M4 Max model. The M5 Max first debuted earlier this year in the MacBook Pro.

The M5 Max features an 18-core CPU, comprising 6 super cores and 12 performance cores. The GPU can be configured with up to 40 cores, with each core integrating a Neural Accelerator. Apple states GPU performance improves by up to 50% compared to the previous generation. Unified memory bandwidth reaches up to 614GB/s, an improvement over the M4 Max generation's maximum of 546GB/s.

The M5 Max Mac Studio comes standard with 36GB of unified memory, with support for up to 128GB. By comparison, the M4 Max Mac Studio originally launched with the same specifications. However, over the past year, due to memory shortages affecting the entire industry, Apple has gradually reduced configuration options. As of yesterday, the M4 Max Mac Studio starts at 36GB of memory, with a maximum of 96GB.

Below are some benchmark figures released by Apple for the M5 Max Mac Studio:

  • LLM prompt processing in LM Studio is up to 10.7 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and 3.9 times faster than M4 Max.
  • Text-to-image generation performance is up to 7.4 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3.5 times faster than M4 Max.
  • Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio is up to 5.3 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3 times faster than M4 Max.
  • Base calling speed for DNA sequencing in Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW is up to 3.5 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 1.9 times faster than M4 Max.

M5 Ultra Mac Studio

The real star of today's announcement is the Mac Studio powered by the M5 Ultra.

The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio offers up to a 36-core CPU, with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, delivering up to 1.3 times faster multi-threaded performance compared to the previous-generation M3 Ultra Mac Studio.

The M5 Ultra features up to an 80-core GPU, which Apple calls the most powerful GPU ever on Apple silicon. This version also brings Neural Accelerators to the Ultra chip for the first time. Neural Accelerators are dedicated hardware built into each GPU core to accelerate AI workloads.

In terms of memory, the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra comes standard with 96GB, configurable up to 512GB—the same as when the M3 Ultra Mac Studio originally launched. However, over the past year, due to memory shortages, Apple significantly cut the M3 Ultra Mac Studio's memory options down to just 96GB. Memory bandwidth reaches up to 1.2TB/s.

The M5 Ultra's media engine features video encoding and decoding engine blocks twice those of the M5 Max, supporting simultaneous processing of up to 33 streams of 8K ProRes video.

Apple released the following benchmark data for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio:

  • CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke is up to 15.4 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 3.3 times faster than M3 Ultra.
  • LLM prompt processing in LM Studio is up to 9.8 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4 times faster than M3 Ultra.
  • Text-to-image generation performance is up to 8.2 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4.3 times faster than M3 Ultra.
  • Scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift is up to 4.7 times faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 1.7 times faster than M3 Ultra.

More Mac Studio specs and details

  • Supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, powered by Apple's in-house N1 networking chip
  • Supports up to 8 external displays, or up to 4 Studio Display XDR at 5K resolution with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Storage performance improved up to 2x due to PCIe Gen 6 support
  • Thunderbolt 5 bandwidth up to 120Gb/s
  • Supports genlock synchronization via USB-C for precise sync of displays with professional cameras

Mac Studio pricing and availability

The Mac Studio with M5 Max starts at US$2,499, with the base configuration including 512GB of storage, priced the same as the M4 Max Mac Studio. The Mac Studio with M5 Ultra starts at US$5,499 with 1TB of storage, US$200 more than the M3 Ultra version.

Buy Mac Studio from Apple:

  • M5 Max Mac Studio: starting at US$2,499 (education price US$2,299)
  • M5 Ultra Mac Studio: starting at US$5,499 (education price US$5,099)

The new Mac Studio lineup is available for pre-order starting today, with deliveries beginning September 22. However, Apple states that the M5 Ultra Mac Studio configured with 512GB of memory "will be available in late October."
